newsitem.title: USA: CSCE trading volume in first half of 1997 rises.
newsitem.headline: CSCE trading volume in first half of 1997 rises.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said on Thursday total trading volume in the first six months of 1997 reached 6,972,356 contracts, a nine-percent increase over the same period in 1996.
Volume in options contracts led the way, jumping by 33 percent in the first half of 1997, while futures trading experienced a four percent increase, the exchange said in a statement.

CSCE said activity in coffee options and futures rose significantly during the period, with overall trading volume in the first six months of 1997 for Coffee "C" calls and puts increasing by 81 percent, to 824,125 contracts. Futures volume rose by 37 percent, to 1,418,873 contracts, compared with the same year ago period.

Overall trading volume for cocoa futures and options declined two and seven percent respectively in the six months to June 1997 compared to the same 1996 period, the exchange said. However, the cocoa futures market saw a large increase in trading during the month of June, with open interest reaching an all-time high of 107,616 contracts on June 30.
Trading in world sugar futures for the first half of the year experienced a five percent decrease in volume, CSCE said, but options on world sugar increased by six percent over the same 1996 period.
